beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley's back, having turned the old band down for good.

options.text: You're still living inside the choice you just made.
This means you made the wrong choice.
The present has nothing to do with that choice.

elaboration: The Lovers doesn't close once you decide — you're still standing inside the choice, and that's exactly what the present position means here.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "So is the Fool card telling me I made the reckless choice by staying on tour?"

options.text: No — it's about what's opening up next, not the choice itself.
Yes, it's confirming you were reckless.
It has nothing to do with what's ahead.

elaboration: The Fool in the future position isn't grading the choice you already made — it's pointing at the fresh start that choice is about to open.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "How does staying with a choice lead to a whole fresh start, though?"

options.text: Committing to it is what clears room for what's next.
It doesn't — the two cards contradict each other.
The Lovers cancels out whatever the Fool says.

elaboration: Standing firmly in the choice is exactly what makes room for the next fresh start — the Lovers settles something so the Fool has somewhere new to go.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "What if I still second-guess it later?"

options.text: That's normal — a real choice gets weighed even after.
You shouldn't ever think about it again.
Second-guessing means the choice was wrong.

elaboration: Weighing every angle isn't a one-time event — the Lovers doesn't mind you circling back to check your own reasoning.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. I think I finally get it — I'm still living inside a choice I already made, and what's next doesn't have to undo it. Thank you for that."
